title: Schneider Electric

lead: In October 2026 Schneider Electric agreed to buy the engineering software maker PTC in an all-cash deal at $205 per share [3]. "The acquisition of PTC represents an important step forward in our ambition to lead the new era of energy and industrial intelligence," CEO Olivier Blum said [4].

items.head: Agrees to acquire PTC
items.text: Schneider announced an all-cash deal valuing PTC at $205 per share; SiliconANGLE reports $23.7 billion and Silicon Republic $22.6 billion [3, 4]. The deal is expected to yield €250 million in annual cost synergies and €800 million in revenue synergies [5].

items.head: Generator-to-chip partnership
items.text: Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants launched a coordinated approach integrating onsite generation, electrical infrastructure and engineering for US data centers [6].

items.head: Hybrid air and liquid CDU
items.text: Schneider's new coolant distribution unit combines fan-wall air cooling with liquid cooling, at up to 3.5 MW of cooling per unit [7].

items.head: New head of Secure Power in Europe
items.text: Schneider appointed Damien Dhellemmes as Senior Vice President of its Secure Power and Data Center business in Europe [8].

items.head: Software-defined medium voltage
items.text: Schneider is extending software-defined architecture into the medium-voltage layer of AI data centers with a standardized switchgear platform [9].

items.head: 800 V DC and cooling
items.text: Schneider's Mike Donahue discussed 800 V DC and its implications for data center cooling as rack power density rises [10].

items.head: Cooling design and local approvals
items.text: Andrew Whitmore, VP of Sales at Motivair by Schneider Electric, writes that community opposition and local approvals are becoming bigger constraints on capacity development [11].

method: Sourced facts only. Identity fields come from the Faraday companies row [1]; Sectors from the Airtable Briefing Library record [2], which links no Theater; every other sentence restates a crawled artifact's recorded summary [3–11]. Where two sources give different deal values, both are shown. No Faraday's Take, no forecast and no call-to-action appear in a Profile. Primary articles were not re-fetched.
